proposals.evidence: DEDR273 gives Kannada avva/avve/abbe mother, Kota av, Kodagu avvë and Gondi avva/avā/avval, with Tamil avvai and Telugu avva. These complete southern survey avv-/abb-/auv- responses fit that mother kinship family, retaining source vowels. The Prakrit avvā comparison and nursery-word character leave the exact transmission history open; divergent Irula agg-/aŋg- forms are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaḷ daughter, Malayalam mōḷ, Kota mōḷ, Kannada magaḷ, Tulu magaḷu, Parji māl and Gadaba māl. The selected survey makaḷ/magaḷ and shortened maka/maga/maha forms are comparative daughter extensions, with southern k/g/h variation and loss of final lateral; Parji/Gadaba māl/malu/melu preserve the separately documented central-Dravidian shape. Source gender/sense and vowel notation are retained; compounds and opaque contractions remain unassigned. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR72 gives Tamil/Malayalam aṭi bottom/base, Kannada aḍi under/bottom and Kodagu aḍi below/down. These simple or locatively inflected southern survey aḍi responses preserve that spatial use; aḍil/aḍiyil/aḍīle and aḍikkɨ retain their case endings and are ordinary inflections rather than separate derivations. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1619 gives Tamil/Malayalam kīḻ below, Kannada kīḻa/keḷagu, Kodagu kïḷï/kïda, Parji kiṛi and Kurux kiyyā beneath. Selected southern kiḷ-/kiś-/kɨg-/kɨh- survey variants and Parji/Gadaba kīḍi(n) are comparative extensions of that lower/below stem; Gadaba is supported comparatively by neighbouring Parji, not directly named in the article. Kurux kiya/kiye retain source final vowels; longer uncertain formations are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5475 explicitly gives Tamil veṭiyal/viṭiyal break of day or dawn, from veṭi/viṭi to dawn. These southern survey vɛḍiyalɛ/vɛḍiyala/bɛḍiyalɛ morning responses preserve the nominal dawn formation, including initial v/b and final vowel variants; they are comparative minority-lect extensions. Questioned Kota/Toda comparisons in the article are not used. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
